name: Electrically Power Assisted Cycle (EPAC)
description: The EU's e-bike: a pedal cycle whose auxiliary electric motor of no more than 250 W assists only while the rider pedals and cuts out by 25 km/h. Excluded from EU type approval, it needs no EU approval, licence or motor insurance, and is sold as machinery under the CE marking; member states set where and how it's ridden.

restrictions.rule: A pedal cycle with pedal assistance from an auxiliary electric motor
The motor's maximum continuous rated power, its maximum 30-minute power at the output shaft, is 250 W or less
The motor cuts out when the cyclist stops pedalling, and otherwise its output is progressively reduced and finally cut off before the cycle reaches 25 km/h
The Regulation makes no exception to the cut-out when pedalling stops, but the harmonised standard EN 15194 allows a start-up (walk) assistance mode that drives it without pedalling up to 6 km/h
Outside EU type approval, so it has no certificate of conformity, which an L-category vehicle needs to be sold or registered
No EU driving licence category covers it: the AM moped licence excludes vehicles with a maximum design speed of 25 km/h or less

Outside the Motor Insurance Directive's compulsory insurance, which covers only motor vehicles propelled exclusively by mechanical power with a maximum design speed over 25 km/h, or over 14 km/h when their net weight is over 25 kg; a member state may still require insurance for it under national law
restrictions.citation: Directive 2009/103/EC, Art. 1(1), as amended by Directive (EU) 2021/2118; Directive (EU) 2021/2118, recitals 4, 6

restrictions.rule: The Court of Justice held that a bicycle whose motor only assists pedalling isn't a vehicle under the Motor Insurance Directive, even with a boost to 20 km/h without pedalling that only muscular power can start
restrictions.citation: Judgment of 12 October 2023, KBC Verzekeringen, C-286/22

restrictions.rule: Machinery under the Machinery Directive, whose exclusion of type-approved two- and three-wheelers doesn't reach it: before sale the manufacturer must meet the Directive's essential health and safety requirements, draw up an EC declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking
Built to EN 15194:2017+A1:2023 it's presumed to meet those requirements, except on vibration, which the standard's listing excludes
restrictions.citation: Directive 2006/42/EC, Art. 7(2); Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1586, Annex I, item 495a

restrictions.rule: The Machinery Regulation replaces the Directive and covers e-bikes outside EU type approval, except for the risks of riding on public roads: the manufacturer must meet its essential health and safety requirements, draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking
